chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام:

For the nose, when its bridge is completely removed, there is the full blood-money. For the eye, when it is put out, there is half of the blood-money. For the ear, when it is cut off, there is half of the blood-money. For the hand, there is half of the blood-money. For the male organ, when it is cut from the place of the glans, there is the full blood-money.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.الذَّكَرِ: the male organ, whose specified severance incurs full diyyah
key_terms.الْأُذُنِ: the ear, whose severance incurs half of the diyyah
key_terms.الْحَشَفَةِ: the glans; the legal point of reference for the injury described
key_terms.الْعَيْنِ: the eye, whose loss incurs half of the diyyah
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, for which half of the diyyah is due

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for injury to the eye, ear, hand, nose, or male organ in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states fixed legal compensations for severe bodily injuries to specific organs. It belongs to the jurisprudence of diyyah, outlining the assessed liability for the loss or removal of bodily members.
